Survey Collections are candidate lidar acquisitions, not FGDB Collections of
Study Areas or Reach Survey Events. Selection expresses intent, not verified
acquisition, download, processing or scientific acceptance.

| Action | Calls | Persistence |
|---|---|---|
| Open | `mod_survey_collections_server` → `store$survey_collections` → `fluvgeo::read_survey_collection_selection` | Offline read of latest snapshot |
| Find | `launch_survey_collection_job` → callr worker → `fluvgeo::discover_survey_collections` | Session result only |
| Inspect/check | Leaflet footprints and server-held candidate keys | No writes |
| Save | `store$save_survey_collections` → `fluvgeo::write_survey_collection_selection` | New sidecar; context and Survey Events unchanged |

The backend queries catalog IDs by envelope, fetches bounded GeoJSON batches,
and intersects footprints using sf. COMPLETE/PARTIAL/FAILED describes each query,
not collection status or confirmed availability. Literal USIEI date/status text
and raw provider attributes remain available for later review. Unknowns are not
filled by inference; cross-catalog identity is not inferred from names or dates.

The worker is cancellable, with a three-minute outer timeout and 30-second HTTP
timeouts. Changing studies disposes it. Progress is indeterminate. Browser inputs
supply candidate keys, not provider URLs or arbitrary file paths. Failed queries
do not clear saved selections. Refresh retains selected records absent from new
responses, including their earlier retrieval evidence.

Saving checks current context and selection revision paths, identity and boundary.
Changing the boundary requires a fresh search. The local snapshot is a planning
artifact, not a final FGDB Survey Collection schema. Event links and acquisition
deduplication must be established explicitly in later work.

## Acquisition planning

`fluvgeo::survey_collection_products` reads retained raw metadata without network
requests. USGS source-DEM and point-cloud links remain separate reported access.
USIEI productsavailable is displayed literally; general access is not proof of
DEM availability. Unknown means unresolved, not unavailable.

Product controls update a session plan of candidate_key/product pairs. Update
acquisition plan stages the choices; Save selections publishes them through the
existing writer with their catalog evidence. DEM and POINT_CLOUD may both be
chosen, including for planned collections. No default, download, scientific
acceptance, Event or cross-catalog merge is implied. DEM acquisition comes first;
point-cloud processing is deferred. Deselecting a collection removes its plan
from the next snapshot, not history. Version 1 snapshots read with an empty plan;
version 2 adds acquisition_plan. Revision/boundary guards are unchanged.

## Shared coverage and resolution review

Discover/select and Plan acquisition are tabs alongside one shared Leaflet map.
`visible_keys()` reads only display mode (inspected, included, custom); it does not
write selection or product state. Product selection updates the inspected record
and zooms that same map. Comparison checkboxes hide/show footprints independently.

The shared backend derives `dem_pixel_size_m` from USGS `dem_gsd_meters` only and
returns a resolution-only screen. The app shows unknowns explicitly. USIEI point
spacing is not raster resolution. Values at most 1 m still require inspection of
downloaded terrain and processing metadata; nothing is marked analysis-ready.

ADR 0007 (`dev/decisions/adr-0007-iterative-terrain-acquisition.md`) records the
iterative acquisition/review workflow and one-or-more source collections per
Survey Event. Current plans are revisable; downloading, review decisions and
Event assembly remain future implementations, not actions performed by Save.

## Implementation routes

- UI/worker: `R/mod_survey_collections.R`.
- Storage/staleness: `R/study_store.R`.
- App tests: `tests/testthat/test-survey-collections.R`.
- Shared provider/spatial/IO methods: sibling `fluvgeo/R/survey_collections.R`;
  backend tests: `fluvgeo/tests/testthat/test_survey_collections.R`.
